q: Who admitted years later that he threw the pizza that hit Sir Alex Ferguson in the Old Trafford tunnel in 2004?
sub: He was 17. Arsenal's 49-game unbeaten run had just ended in a 2-0 defeat.
note: Sky Sports source opened: Fabregas confirmed on air that he threw it, United won 2-0 and the 49-game unbeaten run ended. Born May 1987, so 17 in October 2004. No duplicate in the shipping file.

q: Which West Ham forward caught the ball instead of scoring at Goodison Park in 2000 because the Everton keeper was hurt?
sub: It won him the FIFA Fair Play award. Paul Gerrard was the stricken keeper.
note: Verified on the Di Canio Wikipedia article: December 2000 against Everton, Paul Gerrard down with a twisted knee, FIFA Fair Play Award the following year. Shares an answer with the next row but a different incident.

q: Which Sheffield Wednesday player shoved referee Paul Alcock to the ground after being sent off in 1998?
sub: Eleven-match ban and a ten thousand pound fine. He joined West Ham in January 1999.
note: Event and punishment confirmed (September 1998, eleven games, 10,000 pound fine). The old sub claimed he never played for Wednesday again, which the source does not support, so it now carries the sourced January 1999 West Ham move instead.

q: Which Liverpool striker attacked team mate John Arne Riise with a golf club on a trip to Portugal in 2007?
sub: Days later he scored at Barcelona and celebrated with a golf swing.
note: Wikipedia confirms the Portugal training trip in 2007, the golf club in Riise's room, and the golf swing celebration after scoring at Barcelona.

q: Which Sheffield United substitute was sent off at Reading in 2007 before the ball was even back in play?
sub: He threw an elbow at Stephen Hunt within ten seconds of coming on.
note: Confirmed: 20 January 2007 at Reading, sent off within ten seconds, play had not restarted. The old sub placed it at a throw-in, which the source does not say, so that detail is stripped.

q: Which Manchester United player ended a 1995 press conference with a line about seagulls, a trawler and sardines?
sub: The seagulls follow the trawler because they think sardines will be thrown into the sea.
note: Quote and setting verified on the Cantona Wikipedia article. The eight-month ban was also correct, but it restated the shipping ball row about the kick at the Palace supporter, so the question now rests only on the seagulls line. The vague claim that he later said it meant nothing is gone.

q: Which Arsenal midfielder offered to pay the wages of the club's dinosaur mascot after it was made redundant in 2020?
sub: Jerry Quy had worn the Gunnersaurus suit for 27 years.
note: Al Jazeera source opened: Ozil pledged the mascot's full salary, Jerry Quy had worn the suit for 27 years and had been made redundant in the pandemic cuts.

q: Which club's badger mascot was sent off in 2008 for break-dancing on the pitch after the game had restarted?
sub: Billy the Badger apologised to referee Chris Foy and blamed his hearing and eyesight.
note: Now confirmed on the Fulham article: Billy was sent off against Aston Villa on 3 February 2008 for break-dancing after the referee had restarted play, and apologised to Chris Foy blaming his hearing and eyesight. The badger hearing joke in the old sub is replaced by what the source actually says.

q: Four men were arrested for plotting to black out the floodlights before a 1999 game against Liverpool. At which club's ground?
sub: A Malaysian betting syndicate. An abandoned game would have paid out.
note: Two sources opened confirm four men taken into custody at Charlton in February 1999 with remote sabotage equipment, and that bets would have stood on an abandonment after half-time. Neither source records any jail sentence, so jailed is changed to arrested.

q: Which club's floodlights failed in November 1997, forcing a Premier League game against Crystal Palace to be abandoned?
sub: Part of the same betting scam. West Ham won the rearranged game 4-1 a month later.
note: Wikipedia's match-fixing list ties the November 1997 failure at West Ham to the Malaysian syndicate, and the 1997-98 West Ham season page shows the rearranged Palace fixture on 3 December 1997 won 4-1. The 2-2 scoreline at abandonment is in no source I could open, so it is out.

q: A beach ball thrown from the crowd helped Darren Bent beat which Liverpool goalkeeper at the Stadium of Light in 2009?
sub: The goal stood, Sunderland won 1-0, and the referee was demoted to the Championship.
note: Match article confirms 17 October 2009, Bent, Reina, 1-0, and that Mike Jones was temporarily demoted to the Championship. The old sub said demoted for a week, which no source states.

q: A referee sent off the wrong Arsenal player at Stamford Bridge in 2014 as Chelsea won 6-0. Who was dismissed?
sub: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain had handled it. It was Arsene Wenger's thousandth game in charge.
note: Marriner article confirms Gibbs wrongly sent off for Oxlade-Chamberlain's handball in a 6-0 defeat, and the Wenger article confirms 22 March 2014 was his 1,000th game in charge.

q: Which Manchester United goalkeeper scooped the ball back out from well behind his own line against Tottenham in 2005?
sub: Pedro Mendes shot from 55 yards. No goal was given and it finished 0-0.
note: The 55 yards looked like embroidery but the ghost goal article states it: Mendes shot from 55 yards in the 89th minute, Carroll spilled it a few yards over the line, the game finished goalless.

q: Which Manchester United goalkeeper let a Matt Le Tissier shot roll through his legs in 1999 and played only four league games?
sub: A week later United lost 5-0 at Chelsea. He was sold the following summer.
note: Confirmed: four Premier League appearances, the Le Tissier error on 25 September 1999, the 5-0 at Chelsea on 3 October, sold back to Reggina in July 2000.

q: Which Southampton manager was tricked into signing Ali Dia in 1996 by a caller pretending to be George Weah?
sub: Dia came on for Matt Le Tissier against Leeds and was released within a fortnight.
note: Confirmed: the caller impersonated George Weah, Souness signed him, Dia replaced the injured Le Tissier against Leeds on 23 November 1996 and was released two weeks into his contract.

q: Which winger did Manchester United buy in 2010, a signing Sir Alex Ferguson admitted he had never seen play?
sub: He cost around seven million pounds, five weeks after Vitoria de Guimaraes signed him.
note: I suspected the five weeks was invented. It is not: the article says the United deal was agreed on 11 August 2010, only five weeks after he signed for Vitoria, for a reported 7.4 million pounds, and that Ferguson admitted he had never seen Bebe play.

q: Which Dutch defender played twelve games in four years at Chelsea and refused to leave on forty thousand pounds a week?
sub: Signed in 2000 under Gianluca Vialli, who was gone within weeks. His last game was in 2002.
note: Twelve appearances across 2000 to 2004 and the 40,000 a week are confirmed. The old sub said Vialli signed him and was sacked days later: Wikipedia says the deal was done by the director of football and that Ranieri arrived weeks later, so the sub is softened and the sourced last game, November 2002, added.

q: Which Brazilian signed for Manchester City on deadline day in 2008, hours after being expected to join Chelsea?
sub: From Real Madrid on the day of the Abu Dhabi takeover. He named Chelsea by mistake at his unveiling.
note: The CNN link returns an error, so verified on the Robinho article: 1 September 2008 from Real Madrid, the same day as the Abu Dhabi United Group takeover, and he said Chelsea made a great proposal before correcting himself. The old sub said days after the takeover, which is wrong, and the British record claim is unsourced so it is out.

q: Which defender left Tottenham on a free transfer in 2001 and signed for Arsenal after assuring fans he would stay?
sub: Reporters thought the press conference was to unveil goalkeeper Richard Wright.
note: The Richard Wright twist is real: journalists had been led to believe they were there for Wright's unveiling, and Campbell had made several public assurances he would stay. The source does not date those assurances to January, so that detail is dropped.

q: Which West Bromwich Albion striker drove to Loftus Road on deadline day in 2013 to force through a move that was never agreed?
sub: He was refused entry at Loftus Road and sat outside in his car as the window closed.
note: Sky source opened: January 2013, drove to Loftus Road, no fee agreed, refused entry and left sitting in his car. The sub now says what the source says rather than the car window interviews and being sent home.

q: Which club was docked three points in 1996-97 for calling off a game at Blackburn, and went down by two points?
sub: Bryan Robson said illness and injury left him unable to field a team. They lost both cup finals too.
note: Checked the 1996-97 table: Coventry were safe in 17th on 41, Middlesbrough 19th on 39, so two points is right, as is the deduction for unilaterally postponing the Blackburn game and losing both cup finals. The claim that 23 players were ill or injured is not in the source, so it is stripped.

q: Which club was docked points twice in 2023-24 for breaching the Premier League's financial rules?
sub: Ten points in November, cut to six on appeal, then two more in April. Forest lost four.
note: The old sub was wrong on the first deduction. The season article says ten points on 17 November 2023, reduced to six on appeal in February 2024, then two more on 8 April 2024, with Nottingham Forest docked four.

q: Which club finished the 2007-08 Premier League with eleven points and one win from 38 games?
sub: They scored 20 goals and let in 89, and went 32 league games without a win.
note: Every number checks out on the season page and the 2007-08 league page: 11 points, one win on 17 September 2007, eight draws, 29 defeats, 20 scored, 89 conceded, then 32 games without a win.

q: Which club conceded a hundred goals in their only Premier League season, 1993-94?
sub: Five wins, four clean sheets, and no league win until their seventeenth game.
note: 100 conceded, five wins and four clean sheets all confirmed. Bottom of the table from the third game on is not in the source, so it is replaced by the sourced line that they did not win until their 17th game.

q: Which club finished bottom of the 2015-16 Premier League with seventeen points, exactly half the total of the club above them?
sub: Relegated on 16 April after a 1-0 loss at Manchester United, in the league since 1992.
note: The arithmetic holds: Villa 17, Norwich 19th on 34. Relegation on 16 April after losing 1-0 at Manchester United is sourced, as is their presence since 1992. The four managerial spells in the old sub are not in the source, so they are out.

q: Which club's fans let a chicken loose on the pitch in 2012 as a protest against their poultry-magnate owners?
sub: The hen was draped in club colours. They lost to Wigan that day and went down.
note: Source opened: the hen was draped in the club's colours during the Wigan game at Ewood Park, Blackburn lost 1-0 and were relegated that day. There is no flag reading Out, so that invented detail is gone.

q: Which Manchester City striker's house caught fire from fireworks the night before the 6-1 win at Old Trafford in 2011?
sub: He scored twice the next day and showed a shirt reading Why Always Me.
note: ABC source confirms the firework blaze at his house on the eve of the derby. The match article confirms both goals, at 22 and 60 minutes, and the Why Always Me undershirt revealed after the first.

q: Which Manchester City forward was exiled for six months after Roberto Mancini said he refused to come on at Bayern Munich in 2011?
sub: Tevez called it a misunderstanding. He did not play for City again until March.
note: Confirmed: 27 September 2011 at Bayern, suspension and garden leave, back in training on 14 February 2012 and playing again on 21 March. Wikipedia has Tevez calling it a misunderstanding, not refusing only to warm up, so the sub is corrected.

q: Whose goal at Old Trafford on the final day of 2006-07 kept West Ham up and sent Sheffield United down?
sub: West Ham were fined a record amount over his registration and later settled with Sheffield United.
note: Confirmed on the Tevez article: 13 May 2007, 1-0 at Old Trafford, the record 5.5 million pound fine and the 20 million settlement with Sheffield United in March 2009. Second Tevez answer in the batch, different story.

q: Which manager sat his Hull City players down on the pitch for a half-time dressing down at Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008?
sub: Hull were 4-0 down and he said their 4,000 travelling fans deserved an explanation.
note: Confirmed: 26 December 2008 at Manchester City, 4-0 down at the break, 5-1 at the end, and Brown's own line about the 4,000 travelling fans. The old sub said in front of their own supporters, which reads like a home game.

q: Which Norwich City co-owner took a microphone onto the pitch at half-time in 2005 and called out, let's be having you?
sub: Norwich had led Manchester City 2-0 and ended up losing 3-2.
note: The FourFourTwo page is paywalled, so verified in two parts: the Delia Smith article has the half-time microphone moment against Manchester City in February 2005 and her joint majority shareholding, and the Norwich 2004-05 season page has Ashton on 12 and McKenzie on 16 in a 2-3 defeat.

q: Which Chelsea manager was smuggled into the dressing room in a laundry basket to get round a European touchline ban in 2005?
sub: The kit man carried him in before the Bayern Munich quarter-final.
note: Sky source opened: Mourinho in Chelsea's laundry basket round a two-match UEFA touchline ban at the 2005 Bayern quarter-final, carried by kit man Stewart Bannister. The sub does not name a leg, which is as well since the reports differ on that.

q: Roy Keane was sent off in the 2001 Manchester derby for a tackle on a City midfielder whose son later starred for City. Who?
sub: Keane's book called it deliberate, which cost him five more games and a big fine.
note: Confirmed: April 2001 derby, instant red card, and after his autobiography called it premeditated the FA added a five-game ban and a 150,000 pound fine. Erling Haaland is his son.

q: Which QPR captain was sent off at Manchester City on the final day of 2011-12 and then kicked and tried to headbutt opponents?
sub: Twelve-match ban. City won 3-2 in stoppage time to take the title.
note: Confirmed on the Barton article: captain, elbowed Tevez on 13 May 2012, then kicked Aguero and tried to headbutt Kompany, twelve-match ban and a 75,000 pound fine. City won 3-2.

q: Which club's fans ran onto the pitch before the whistle in 2022 after coming from 2-0 down against Crystal Palace to stay up?
sub: Dominic Calvert-Lewin headed the 3-2 winner with five minutes left.
note: Sky report opened: 2-0 down to Mateta and Ayew, Keane 54, Richarlison 75, Calvert-Lewin's header on 85, fans on the pitch before the final whistle as well as after, and survival secured.

q: Which goalkeeper became the first to score in the Premier League, for Aston Villa at Goodison Park in 2001?
sub: A 90th-minute volley from a corner. Villa lost 3-2 anyway.
note: Confirmed as the first goalkeeper goal in the Premier League: 20 October 2001 at Everton, a volley from a 90th-minute corner, Villa beaten 3-2. The old sub named Paul Gerrard as the keeper beaten, which no source I opened supports, and stoppage time is wrong for a 90th-minute goal.

q: Which Stoke City goalkeeper scored with a clearance after thirteen seconds against Southampton in 2013?
sub: Measured at 91.9 metres and recognised by Guinness as the longest goal scored.
note: Confirmed: 2 November 2013, 13 seconds in, 91.9 metres, a Guinness world record in 2014. Wind-assisted is commentary rather than source, so the sourced thirteen seconds carries the question instead.

q: Which goalkeeper headed a winner in the last minute of stoppage time at West Bromwich Albion in May 2021?
sub: The first Premier League keeper to score with a header, and the first to win a game with one.
note: Confirmed: 16 May 2021, 95th minute header, 2-1 win, first headed goal by a goalkeeper in the Premier League and the first match-winning one.

q: Manchester United changed shirts at half-time at the Dell in 1996, saying the players could not see each other. What colour had they worn?
sub: They were 3-0 down at the break, lost 3-1, and never wore the kit again.
note: Sky source opened: grey shirts swapped for blue and white at half-time, 3-0 down at the break, 3-1 at the end, Ferguson said the players could not pick each other out, and the kit was never worn again.

q: Which club played the 2013-14 Premier League season in red after an owner replaced their traditional blue home shirt?
sub: Vincent Tan's rebrand ran from 2012 until January 2015, dragon crest and all.
note: Confirmed on the Cardiff City article: red from 2012, badge redesigned around the Welsh dragon, back to blue on 9 January 2015 after three seasons in red, 2013-14 among them.

q: Which club's splattered yellow and green home shirt of the early 1990s was nicknamed the bird poo kit?
sub: They wore it while finishing third in the first Premier League season.
note: Source opened: the 1992-94 Ribero kit is the one known as the bird poo kit, and the 1992-93 league page confirms Norwich finished third.

q: Which club's owner tried to rename them the Tigers, only for the Football Association to throw the plan out in 2014?
sub: Assem Allam wanted Hull Tigers for the wider market and said he would appeal.
note: Confirmed: the FA Council rejected the change on 9 April 2014 and Allam wanted Hull Tigers for national and international use and said he would appeal. The two to one vote margin in the old sub is in no source, so it is out.

q: Which club came back from 4-0 down at half-time to draw 4-4 with Arsenal in February 2011?
sub: Joey Barton scored two penalties after Abou Diaby was sent off.
note: Sky report opened: 5 February 2011, Arsenal 4-0 up at the break, Diaby sent off on 50, Barton penalties on 68 and 83, Best 75, Tiote 87.

q: Which substitute scored a hat-trick to earn West Bromwich Albion a 5-5 draw in Sir Alex Ferguson's last match in 2013?
sub: Manchester United led 5-2 after 63 minutes, then shipped three in the last ten.
note: Match report opened: Lukaku was a second-half substitute, United led 5-2 from Hernandez on 63, then West Brom scored on 80, 81 and 86. The old sub said United led 5-2 with nine minutes to go, which is a minute out, so the sub now uses the timings.

q: Which club lost a Premier League game 9-0 twice, at home to Leicester City in 2019 and at Manchester United in 2021?
sub: The Leicester result was the biggest away win in the league's history.
note: Confirmed: 25 October 2019 at St Mary's, a record away win in the English top flight, and 2 February 2021 at Old Trafford, both 9-0, Southampton the first club to lose as such twice.

q: Which two clubs produced eleven goals in one Premier League game in September 2007?
sub: Portsmouth won 7-4 at Fratton Park.
note: The 2007-08 league page calls it the highest-scoring match in Premier League history: Portsmouth 7-4 Reading on 29 September 2007 at Fratton Park.

q: Which Tottenham striker scored five goals in a 9-1 win over Wigan Athletic in November 2009?
note: Confirmed on the Premier League records article: Defoe five in Tottenham 9-1 Wigan, 22 November 2009, one of only five players to score five in a match.

q: Which Liverpool striker scored in stoppage time to win the 4-3 against Newcastle United in April 1996?
sub: Kevin Keegan sagged over the advertising hoardings as Anfield went up.
note: Match article opened: Collymore scored in the second minute of stoppage time on 3 April 1996 and the article itself describes Keegan slumped over the advertising hoardings.

q: Which club came from 3-0 down in the closing minutes to draw 3-3 with Liverpool in May 2014?
sub: Liverpool were trying to eat into Manchester City's goal difference. City took the title.
note: The 3-0 lead pegged back to 3-3 at Selhurst Park on 5 May 2014 is confirmed on the Liverpool season page, along with the goal difference chase and City's title. The exact eleven-minute window and the image of Suarez in tears are not in any source I opened, so both are replaced.

q: Which club beat Manchester United 7-0 in March 2023?
sub: Mohamed Salah, Cody Gakpo and Darwin Nunez all scored twice at Anfield.
note: Liverpool's 2022-23 season page confirms 5 March 2023 at Anfield with braces for Gakpo, Nunez and Salah plus a Firmino goal, their biggest ever win over United.

q: Which club won the first Premier League season, in 1992-93?
sub: Their first league title in 26 years.
note: The 1992-93 season page states it was the club's first title in 26 years. Not in the shipping file, which only has the Ferguson thirteen-titles question.

q: Which club won the Premier League in 2024-25?
sub: Their second title of the Premier League era, five years after the first.
note: Confirmed on the Premier League champions list: Liverpool 2019-20 and 2024-25, so second of the era and five years on.

q: Which club won the Premier League in 2025-26, ending a wait of twenty-two years?
sub: Their first league title since the Invincibles of 2003-04.
note: Post-cutoff, so checked twice: the Premier League article and the Arsenal article both have the title sealed on 19 May 2026, a 22-year wait since 2003-04, their fourth Premier League title. Matches the shipping file, which has City second in 2025-26.

q: Which club won four Premier League titles in a row from 2020-21 to 2023-24?
note: Champions list confirms City in 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24.

q: Which club won the Premier League in 2013-14 under Manuel Pellegrini?
note: Confirmed on the list of title-winning managers: Pellegrini, Manchester City, 2013-14.

q: Which club won the Premier League in 2016-17 under Antonio Conte?
note: Confirmed on the list of title-winning managers: Conte, Chelsea, 2016-17.

q: Which club won the Premier League three seasons in a row from 2006-07 to 2008-09?
note: Champions list confirms United in all three. Different answer from the shipping hard row about who managed both three-in-a-row runs, so not a duplicate.

q: Which club plays its home games at Anfield?
note: List of Premier League stadiums confirms Anfield as Liverpool's and not shared.

q: Which club plays its home games at Old Trafford?
note: List of Premier League stadiums confirms Old Trafford as Manchester United's and not shared. The cricket ground of the same name is not a football club, so the answer stays single.

q: Which club plays its home games at the Etihad Stadium?
note: List of Premier League stadiums confirms the Etihad as Manchester City's and not shared.

q: Which club plays its home games at Villa Park?
note: List of Premier League stadiums confirms Villa Park as Aston Villa's and not shared.

q: Which club plays its home games at St James' Park?
note: List of Premier League stadiums confirms St James' Park as Newcastle's and not shared. Exeter City's ground is spelled without the apostrophe and is nowhere near this deck, so the reader will not have to judge it.

q: Which club is nicknamed the Gunners?
note: Arsenal article confirms the Gunners as the club nickname.

q: Which club is nicknamed the Toffees?
note: Everton article confirms the Toffees, after the Mother Noblett's toffee shop in Everton village.

q: Which club is nicknamed the Hammers?
note: West Ham article confirms the Hammers, alongside the Irons, from the club's works-team roots.

q: Which club is nicknamed the Eagles?
note: Palace article confirms the Eagles, adopted by Malcolm Allison in 1973 and on the badge. No other English club carries it.

q: How many clubs play in the Premier League in a season?
note: Premier League article: 20 clubs. Not a record claim, so the present tense is safe.

q: How many league games does each Premier League club play in a season?
note: Premier League article: each team plays 38 matches, home and away against the other 19.

q: In which year did the Premier League replace the First Division as England's top flight?
note: Premier League article confirms the 1992 founding, replacing the First Division as the top tier.

q: Which Dutchman took over as Liverpool manager in 2024?
sub: He won the league in his first season.
note: Slot article confirms Dutch, appointed 1 June 2024 in place of Klopp, and the title clinched on 27 April 2025 in his first season.

q: Which manager ended Arsenal's long wait for a league title in 2025-26?
sub: Three straight seasons as runners-up came first.
note: Post-cutoff fact checked on the Arteta article and the Premier League news piece: his first title, and it followed three consecutive runners-up seasons. Different answer from the shipping row about his 2019 appointment.

q: Which Norwegian managed Manchester United from 2018 to 2021?
note: Confirmed: Norwegian, caretaker from 19 December 2018, permanent from March 2019, sacked in November 2021.

q: Which German manager won the Champions League with Chelsea in 2021?
note: Confirmed: German, Chelsea manager from January 2021, beat Manchester City 1-0 in the final on 29 May 2021.

q: Which club did Pep Guardiola manage before joining Manchester City?
note: Confirmed: Bayern Munich from 2013 to 2016, then City from the start of 2016-17.

q: Which club did Jurgen Klopp manage before joining Liverpool?
note: Confirmed: Borussia Dortmund from 2008 to 2015, Liverpool from 8 October 2015.

q: Which Australian became Tottenham Hotspur manager in 2023?
note: Confirmed: announced on 6 June 2023, starting 1 July, and the article calls him the first Australian to manage in the Premier League. Greek-born but raised in Melbourne, so the reader will not get a second defensible answer.

q: Which club did Harry Kane join from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023?
note: Confirmed on the list of most expensive transfers: Tottenham to Bayern Munich, 2023.

q: Which club did Declan Rice join from West Ham United in 2023?
note: Confirmed on the list of most expensive transfers: West Ham to Arsenal, 2023.

q: Which club did Wayne Rooney join from Everton in 2004?
note: Rooney article confirms the move from Everton to Manchester United in 2004 for an initial 20 million pounds.

q: Which club did Manchester City sign Erling Haaland from in 2022?
note: Haaland article confirms the release clause triggered on 10 May 2022 and the Dortmund to City move completed that July.

q: Which club did Liverpool sign Virgil van Dijk from in January 2018?
note: Van Dijk article confirms the January 2018 window, from Southampton, a reported 75 million pounds.

q: Which club did Jack Grealish leave for Manchester City in 2021?
note: Confirmed on the list of most expensive transfers: Aston Villa to Manchester City, 2021.

q: Which club did Manchester United sign Eric Cantona from in 1992?
note: Cantona article confirms Leeds to United on 26 November 1992 for one million pounds.

q: Which club did Arsenal sign Dennis Bergkamp from in 1995?
note: Bergkamp article confirms Inter to Arsenal in June 1995 for about 7.5 million pounds, Bruce Rioch's first signing.

q: Which striker scored 260 Premier League goals for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United?
note: Records article confirms Shearer on 260, the all-time top scorer, and all 260 came at Blackburn and Newcastle since his Southampton years predate the Premier League. Phrased in the past, so it does not go stale.

q: Which forward won the Golden Boot in 2003-04, 2004-05 and 2005-06?
note: Duplicate. The shipping easy deck already has which Frenchman won the Premier League Golden Boot four times with Arsenal, answer Thierry Henry. Same fact, same answer, same tier, so this is a reword.

q: Which Manchester City striker scored five goals against Newcastle United in October 2015?
note: Records article confirms Aguero five in Manchester City 6-1 Newcastle on 3 October 2015.

q: Which Manchester United striker scored a hat-trick in the 8-2 win over Arsenal in August 2011?
note: Rooney article confirms the hat-trick in the 8-2 against Arsenal in late August 2011, his 150th United goal being the first of them.

q: Which forward returned to Manchester United in 2021 and was their leading league scorer that season?
note: Season page confirms he rejoined on 27 August 2021 and was United's leading Premier League scorer with 18.

q: How many clubs are relegated from the Premier League at the end of a season?
sub: They drop into the Championship.
note: The 2025-26 season page shows exactly three going down, West Ham, Burnley and Wolves, to the EFL Championship, and the list of clubs shows the same pattern throughout.

q: Which club came from 2-0 down against Aston Villa on the final day of 2021-22 to win the title?
sub: Three goals in five minutes, with Ilkay Gundogan scoring twice.
note: The City season page puts it exactly as the sub does: three goals in five minutes including a Gundogan brace, after Cash and Coutinho had put Villa 2-0 up.

q: Which club won the Premier League and the Champions League in the same season in 2022-23?
sub: They added the FA Cup for a treble.
note: City's 2022-23 season page confirms all three: league on 20 May, FA Cup on 3 June, Champions League on 10 June.

q: Arsenal's Premier League titles came in 1997-98, 2001-02, 2003-04 and which other season?
note: Internal mirror. The easy row asking which club won the Premier League in 2025-26 is the same fact inverted, and this batch is meant to feed the one-point end, so the easy version is the keeper. The fact itself is correct: Arsenal have four, the other three being 1997-98, 2001-02 and 2003-04.

q: Which two clubs had won the Premier League exactly once each by the end of 2024-25?
note: Premier League article lists Blackburn and Leicester on one title each, with Liverpool on two after 2024-25. Properly anchored, and it asks for a pair rather than rewording either shipping single-club row.

q: Which club was the first to retain the Premier League title, winning it again in 1993-94?
note: Champions list confirms United in both 1992-93 and 1993-94, so the first to retain it.

q: Who scored the first goal in Premier League history, for Sheffield United in August 1992?
sub: Against Manchester United, who lost 2-1.
note: Deane article confirms the first Premier League goal, after five minutes on 15 August 1992, in a 2-1 win over Manchester United.

q: Which Southampton forward scored a hat-trick in under three minutes against Aston Villa in 2015?
sub: Two minutes and 56 seconds, a Premier League record when he did it.
note: Records article confirms 2 minutes 56 seconds in Southampton 6-1 Aston Villa on 16 May 2015. The old sub called it the fastest in the competition's history in the present tense, which the brief throws out, so it is anchored to when he did it.

q: Which Southampton striker scored at Watford in April 2019 in under eight seconds from the kick-off?
note: Records article confirms 7.69 seconds against Watford on 23 April 2019. Left at normal: the question hands over the club and the date and the record is well known, so a regular watcher would not be stuck.

q: Which Leicester City striker scored in eleven consecutive Premier League games in 2015-16?
note: Vardy article confirms the eleven-game run in 2015-16, which passed van Nistelrooy's mark, ending at Swansea on 5 December 2015.

q: Which Bulgarian scored five goals for Manchester United against Blackburn Rovers in 2010?
note: Records article confirms Berbatov five in United 7-1 Blackburn on 27 November 2010.

q: Which Manchester United striker scored five goals in the 9-0 win over Ipswich Town in 1995?
note: Records article confirms Cole five in United 9-0 Ipswich on 4 March 1995.

q: Which Portuguese manager took charge of Manchester United in November 2024?
sub: He came from Sporting CP.
note: Amorim article confirms Portuguese, in charge at United from 11 November 2024, straight from Sporting CP.

q: Which manager took Tottenham Hotspur into the Champions League for the first time, finishing fourth in 2009-10?
note: Redknapp article confirms fourth on 70 points in 2009-10 and the resulting Champions League play-off, their first time in the competition.

q: Which manager spent eight seasons at Bolton Wanderers before taking over at Newcastle United in 2007?
